## Statement

Let $U$ be a smooth Lorentzian four-dimensional chart domain with metric $g$ as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]], and let $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ be constant. Write $\Omega^k(U)$ for the smooth real $k$-forms on $U$. Here $d:\Omega^k(U)\to\Omega^{k+1}(U)$, $0\le k\le3$, is the exterior derivative with coordinate formula $(d\beta)_{a_0\ldots a_k}=(k+1)\partial_{[a_0}\beta_{a_1\ldots a_k]}$, and $\star_g:\Omega^2(U)\to\Omega^2(U)$ is the Lorentzian Hodge map characterized by $\alpha\wedge\star_g\beta=\frac12\alpha_{ab}\beta^{ab}\,\operatorname{vol}_g$ for $\alpha,\beta\in\Omega^2(U)$, as in [[lem-emg-lorentz-hodge-calculus]]. Both operators are real-linear. Suppose $G_{ab}(g)+\Lambda g_{ab}=0$. Let $F_1\in\Omega^2(U)$ satisfy $dF_1=0$ and $d(\star_gF_1)=0$. For any real dimensionless $\varepsilon$, put $F_\varepsilon:=\varepsilon F_1$ and define

$$T^{(1)}_{ab}:=\mu_0^{-1}\mathcal Q_{ab}(g,F_1),\qquad \mathscr R_{ab}(g,F;\Lambda):=G_{ab}(g)+\Lambda g_{ab}-\frac{\kappa}{\mu_0}\mathcal Q_{ab}(g,F),$$

using $\kappa,\mu_0,\mathcal Q$ of [[def-emg-geometric-scaling]] and [[thm-emg-field-normalization-equivalence]]. Then $F_\varepsilon$ remains an exact source-free Maxwell field on the fixed metric and

$$\mathscr R_{ab}(g,F_\varepsilon;\Lambda)=-\kappa\varepsilon^2T^{(1)}_{ab}.$$

For a smooth covariant two-tensor $S$ and compact $K\subset U$, define the chart component norm of its restriction by $\|S\|_{K}:=\max_{0\le a,b\le3}\sup_{p\in K}|S_{ab}(p)|$ when $K\ne\varnothing$. In this estimate and its applications, use $\sup_{p\in\varnothing}f(p):=0$ for nonnegative component functions $f$; equivalently, the empty restriction has $\|S\|_{\varnothing}:=0$. It is finite for smooth $S$ and satisfies

$$\|\mathscr R(g,F_\varepsilon;\Lambda)\|_K=\kappa\varepsilon^2\|T^{(1)}\|_K.$$

If $\varepsilon\ne0$ and $T^{(1)}$ is not identically zero on $K$, the fixed pair $(g,F_\varepsilon)$ is not an exact coupled Einstein–Maxwell solution on $K$. This is a residual estimate only; it gives no nearby metric, solution-distance bound, point-source solution or backreaction limit.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The smooth Lorentzian geometry of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]], positive constants and quadratic tensor of [[def-emg-geometric-scaling]], a compact chart subset $K$, and the stated vacuum and source-free equations. The inherited geometric setup carries $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as in [A1].

[F1] The tensor $\mathcal Q_{ab}(g,F)$ is quadratic in the two-form and the Einstein normalization uses the coefficient $\kappa/\mu_0$. ([[thm-emg-field-normalization-equivalence]])

[F2] The geometric setup admits smooth two-forms; the specified $F_1$ is smooth on $U$. ([[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]])

[F3] The exterior derivative on smooth forms is real-linear, and the Lorentzian Hodge map is a real-linear bundle map characterized by $\alpha\wedge\star_g\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g\operatorname{vol}_g$, with $\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g=\frac12\alpha_{ab}\beta^{ab}$ on two-forms. ([[lem-emg-lorentz-hodge-calculus]])

[A1] The inherited choice assumption is Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, not full Choice. ([[def-countable-choice]])

## Proof

1.1 Exterior differentiation and the Hodge map are real-linear by [F3], so $dF_\varepsilon=\varepsilon dF_1=0$ and $d(\star_gF_\varepsilon)=\varepsilon d(\star_gF_1)=0$. Thus the source-free Maxwell equations remain exactly satisfied on the unchanged $g$. [given, F2, F3, A1, algebra]

1.2 Each term of $\mathcal Q$ is quadratic in $F$, so $\mathcal Q(g,F_\varepsilon)=\varepsilon^2\mathcal Q(g,F_1)$ and the associated lower tensor is $\varepsilon^2T^{(1)}$ by the definition in the Statement. [given, F1, algebra]

2.1 Substituting the assumed vacuum equation $G(g)+\Lambda g=0$ and step 1.2 into the residual definition gives $\mathscr R(g,F_\varepsilon;\Lambda)=-\kappa\varepsilon^2T^{(1)}$ exactly. [given, F1, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 If $K=\varnothing$, the stated convention makes both norms in the claimed equality zero. Suppose $K\ne\varnothing$. Each component $f=S_{ab}|_K$ is continuous; the relative open sets $f^{-1}((-n,n))$, for positive integers $n$, cover $K$. Compactness gives a finite subcover, and the largest of its indices bounds $|f|$ on $K$. Thus every component supremum, and hence their finite maximum, is finite. The norm is homogeneous, so step 2.1 and $\kappa\varepsilon^2\ge0$ give $\|\mathscr R\|_K=\kappa\varepsilon^2\|T^{(1)}\|_K$. If $\varepsilon\ne0$ and $T^{(1)}$ is not identically zero on $K$, then $K$ is nonempty and some component of $T^{(1)}$ is nonzero at a point of $K$; step 2.1 makes the residual nonzero there, so the fixed pair fails the coupled equation on $K$. No estimate comparing it with a different metric follows from this identity. [given, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Let $D\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}$, let $\phi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^D;\mathbb R)$ (the smooth real-valued functions with compact support), let $r\ge3$ be an integer, and let $g_r\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$. The Euclidean gradient is $\nabla_E\phi:=(\partial_1\phi,\ldots,\partial_D\phi)$ and its squared norm is $|\nabla_E\phi|^2:=\sum_{j=1}^D(\partial_j\phi)^2$. With Lebesgue measure $d^Dx$ on $\mathbb R^D$, define the real-valued functionals

$$S_{\mathrm{kin}}(\phi):=\frac12\int_{\mathbb R^D}|\nabla_E\phi(x)|^2\,d^Dx,\qquad S_r(\phi):=g_r\int_{\mathbb R^D}\phi(x)^r\,d^Dx.$$

They are finite because $\phi$ and its derivatives have compact support. Use the following formal natural-unit mass-degree convention: set $\hbar=c=1$, assign degree $-1$ to each coordinate $x^\mu$ ($1\le\mu\le D$), degree $1$ to each partial derivative, and degree $-D$ to $d^Dx$; degrees add under products. Normalize both displayed functionals as dimensionless action terms of degree $0$. The symbols $[\phi]$ and $[g_r]$ denote their formal mass degrees in this convention; these are the engineering dimensions. They are $[\phi]=(D-2)/2$ and $[g_r]=D-r(D-2)/2$. Under the dilation $\phi_b(x)=b^{-(D-2)/2}\phi(x/b)$ for $b>0$, $S_{\mathrm{kin}}(\phi_b)=S_{\mathrm{kin}}(\phi)$ and $S_r(\phi_b)=b^{D-r(D-2)/2}S_r(\phi)$. Call the monomial relevant, marginal, or irrelevant at tree level according as this dilation exponent is positive, zero, or negative. Thus a quartic monomial has exponent $4-D$: it is relevant for $D<4$, marginal by engineering dimension for $D=4$, and irrelevant for $D>4$. These labels concern only this classical engineering-dimension convention; no quantum correction, fixed point, or renormalization-group flow is asserted.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** $D\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}$, $b>0$, $\phi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^D;\mathbb R)$, integer $r\ge3$, and real scalar $g_r\ne0$.

[A1] The statement's formal natural-unit mass-degree convention assigns $[x^\mu]=-1$, $[\partial_\mu]=1$, $[d^Dx]=-D$, and degree $0$ to both $S_{\mathrm{kin}}$ and $S_r$; degrees add under products, with $\hbar=c=1$.

[A2] The specified functionals are the Lebesgue integrals of the Euclidean-gradient and monomial densities in the statement; compact support makes both integrals finite.

## Proof

**Given:** The dimension convention [A1] and the functionals and domain in [A2].

1.1 Since $S_{\mathrm{kin}}$ has degree $0$ and $d^Dx$ has degree $-D$, its integrand $|\nabla_E\phi|^2$ has degree $D$. Each Euclidean partial derivative contributes degree $1$, so $2+2[\phi]=D$ and $[\phi]=(D-2)/2$. [given, A1, A2, algebra]

1.2 By the chain rule, $\partial_j(\phi_b)(x)=b^{-(D-2)/2-1}(\partial_j\phi)(x/b)$ for each $j=1,\ldots,D$. With $x=by$, Lebesgue measure contributes $b^D$ and the two differentiated fields contribute $b^{-(D-2)-2}=b^{-D}$, so $S_{\mathrm{kin}}(\phi_b)=S_{\mathrm{kin}}(\phi)$. [given, A2, algebra]

2.1 By [A1], $S_r$ has degree $0$, so its integrand $g_r\phi^r$ must have degree $D$. Therefore $[g_r]+r[\phi]=D$, and substituting step 1.1 gives $[g_r]=D-r(D-2)/2$. [given, A1, A2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 For the monomial, the same Lebesgue change of variables gives $S_r(\phi_b)=g_r b^D b^{-r(D-2)/2}\int\phi(y)^r d^Dy=b^{D-r(D-2)/2}S_r(\phi)$. At $r=4$ the exponent is $4-D$, whose sign gives the stated relevant, marginal, or irrelevant tree-level label. [given, A1, A2, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and the selected free-field model of
[[post-qft-free-field-model]], using the metric, length coordinates, inverse-
length parameter $\mu\ge0$, field dimensions and Clifford convention fixed by
[[def-qft-framework-units]]. The classical scalar field
$\phi_{\mathrm n}:\mathbb R^4\to\mathbb R$ is smooth and real; the classical
Dirac field $\psi_{\mathrm n}:\mathbb R^4\to\mathbb C^4$ is smooth with
commuting components. Their adopted free actions are the scalar and Dirac
functionals stated in [[post-qft-free-field-model]]. Action symbols are used
only through compactly supported smooth variations, so no global
integrability of the classical background fields is assumed.

The compact-variation stationarity equations are
$$(\Box-\mu^2)\phi_{\mathrm n}=0,\qquad (i\gamma^a\partial_a-\mu)\psi_{\mathrm n}=0,$$
with $\Box=-\partial_0^2+\Delta_{\mathbf x}$. In the separately adopted
scalar and Dirac Fock representations, the corresponding weak test equations
are, for $f\in\mathscr S(\mathbb R^4)$ and
$F\in\mathscr S(\mathbb R^4;\mathbb C^4)$,
$$\Phi_\mu((\Box-\mu^2)f)=0,\qquad \Psi\!\left((i\partial_0-h_D(-i\nabla))F\right)=0.$$
Here “weak test equation” means precisely that smearing the constructed field
with the displayed differential operator gives the zero operator on its
stated common domain. With $h_D(\mathbf k)=\boldsymbol\alpha\cdot\mathbf k+\beta\mu$,
$\gamma^0=\beta$, and $\gamma^j=\beta\alpha^j$ as adopted in
[[post-qft-free-field-model]], the Dirac test operator is equivalent to
$i\gamma^a\partial_a-\mu$.

Thus the classical action equations and the tested equations of the selected
free representations have the same differential expressions at these
normalizations. The Fock representation, species/statistics assignments and
vacua are additional physical model assumptions; they are not deductions from
the classical actions. No empirical outcome or measurement is asserted.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the fixed QFT unit and Clifford conventions,
the adopted classical actions and free representations, and the current draft
mathematical carriers for the variation and test-restriction arguments.

[A1] Countable Choice, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, means every sequence of
nonempty sets has a choice function. [[def-countable-choice]]

[F1] [[def-qft-framework-units]] fixes $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$,
$x^0=ct$, $\Box=\eta^{ab}\partial_a\partial_b$, inverse-length $\mu$,
$\{\gamma^a,\gamma^b\}=-2\eta^{ab}I_4$, and the length dimensions of the
scalar and Dirac fields.

[F2] [[post-qft-free-field-model]] adopts the displayed scalar and commuting
Dirac actions, the selected scalar bosonic and Dirac particle/antiparticle CAR
Fock representations, their vacua, and the explicit $h_D,\beta,\gamma^a$
conventions. These are physical model assumptions, not mathematical
consequences of the actions.

[F3] [[lem-qft-free-action-equations]] assumes smooth real scalar and smooth
commuting complex spinor fields, with compactly supported smooth variations.
It states the exact first-variation identities, that no global action
integrability is assumed, and that stationarity under all such variations is
equivalent to the pointwise Klein–Gordon and Dirac equations. Its current
Step 1 receipt is ready for this draft mathematical carrier; independent
review is still pending.

[F4] [[lem-qft-mass-shell-test-restriction-continuity]] states, for every
$\mu\ge0$ and Schwartz test $f$,
$K_\mu((\partial_0^2-\Delta+\mu^2)f)=0$. Its current Step 1 receipt is ready
for this draft mathematical carrier; the containing QFT-MF02 page remains a
draft prerequisite.

[F5] [[lem-qft-smeared-free-scalar]] defines
$\Phi_\mu(f)=a(K_\mu\overline f)+a^\dagger(K_\mu f)$ on the finite-particle
domain and its test-function convention. The field carrier remains draft and
its upstream QFT-MF01 dependencies are unresolved, so this representation is
used conditionally.

[F6] [[lem-qft-free-dirac-car-locality]] defines the bounded CAR field
$\Psi(F)=c(P_+u_F)+c^\dagger(\overline{P_-u_F})$ on its stated Fock space.
Its current Step 1 decision is escalated through QFT-MF01/MF02 dependencies,
so this field map is used conditionally.

[F7] [[lem-qft-free-dirac-car-locality]] proves
$u_{(i\partial_0-h_D(-i\nabla))F}=0$ for Schwartz spinor tests. This tested
equation is conditional on the escalated field and upstream carriers.

## Proof

**Given:** [A1] and [F1]–[F7].

1.1 By [F3], for each compactly supported smooth real variation $h$ and
compactly supported smooth spinor variation $\chi$, the first variations of
the displayed actions are the stated integrals against
$(\Box-\mu^2)\phi_{\mathrm n}$ and
$(i\gamma^a\partial_a-\mu)\psi_{\mathrm n}$. The lemma proves both
necessity and sufficiency of the displayed pointwise equations for
stationarity under all such variations; this step uses the commuting
classical spinor convention of [F2]. [A1, F2, F3, given]

1.2 Since $\Box-\mu^2=-(\partial_0^2-\Delta+\mu^2)$, [F4] and linearity
give $K_\mu((\Box-\mu^2)f)=0$ for every Schwartz $f$. The differential
operator has real coefficients, so the same identity holds for $\overline f$.
The scalar field formula in [F5] applies $a$ and $a^\dagger$ only to
$K_\mu\overline f$ and $K_\mu f$; both vanish for $f$ replaced by
$(\Box-\mu^2)f$. Hence the constructed scalar field satisfies the stated
weak test equation. [F1, F4, F5, algebra]

1.3 By [F7], the one-particle vector of
$(i\partial_0-h_D(-i\nabla))F$ is zero. Substitution in the bounded CAR
field formula in [F6] makes both its creation and annihilation terms zero,
so the corresponding smeared field is zero. From [F2],
$$\beta(i\partial_0-h_D(-i\nabla))=i\beta\partial_0+i\beta\alpha^j\partial_j-\mu=i\gamma^a\partial_a-\mu,$$
using $\beta^2=I_4$. Thus this is exactly the tested Dirac differential
expression in the classical equation of [F3]. [F1, F2, F3, F6, F7, algebra]

2.1 The quantum representations used in steps 1.2 and 1.3 enter only through
the physical adoption [F2]; steps 1.1–1.3 establish equation agreement under
that adoption and do not construct or derive the representation from the
classical action. The conclusion is therefore conditional on the selected
free model and carries no empirical or general quantization claim. [F2,
step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, given] ∎

## Statement

Assume the fixed finite-graph model adopted by
[[post-qft-compact-lattice-gauge-model]]: a finite nonempty oriented graph,
$s\ge1$ finite CAR modes per vertex, fixed backgrounds
$b_x\in\{0,\ldots,s\}$, link electric operators $E_e$, the joint Gauss
operators $G_x$, and $H=H_0+V_B+V_F$ on the exact maximal domain
$D(H_0)$ of [[def-qft-compact-lattice-gauge-data]]. Assume the Axiom of Choice
and a constant $\hbar>0$ in joule-seconds. Then the physical sector
$$\mathcal H_{\rm phys}=\bigcap_{x\in V}\ker G_x$$
is nonzero. The restriction $H_{\rm phys}:=H|_{D(H)\cap\mathcal H_{\rm phys}}$
is self-adjoint, and
$$\mathcal U_{\rm phys}(t)=e^{-itH_{\rm phys}/\hbar},\qquad t\in\mathbb R,$$
is a strongly continuous unitary group on $\mathcal H_{\rm phys}$ with the
exact derivative domain $D(H)\cap\mathcal H_{\rm phys}$. This is an exact
fixed-regulator result conditional on the stated mathematical suppliers; it
asserts no continuum dynamics or continuum QED construction.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Full AC, the adopted finite-graph model, its CAR/Fourier conventions, the self-adjoint gauge-sector construction, and $\hbar>0$.

[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: every family of nonempty sets has a choice function. In particular it supplies the Countable Choice assumption in the finite-graph definition.

[L1] [[def-countable-choice]]: Countable Choice selects one element from each set in a sequence of nonempty sets. The finite-graph definition uses this weaker assumption for its conditional Fock/CAR construction.

[F1] [[post-qft-compact-lattice-gauge-model]]: the physical model adopts the finite oriented graph, compact rotor links, finite CAR matter, fixed backgrounds, and exact Hamiltonian/domain of [[def-qft-compact-lattice-gauge-data]]. Its CAR inputs remain draft suppliers; the postulate does not call them independently accepted.

[F2] [[lem-qft-lattice-gauss-projection]]: on the current draft interface the maximal diagonal Gauss operators have a nonzero joint kernel; for each allowed background, the zero-link Fourier vector tensored with an occupation vector having $b_x$ occupied modes at each vertex is a normalized vector in that kernel. The carrier and its complete conditional proof have a current Step-1 ready record; that record is not proof acceptance.

[F3] [[lem-qft-lattice-physical-evolution]]: for the same model data and full AC, $H$ is self-adjoint on $D(H_0)$, $e^{-itH/\hbar}$ is strongly continuous, commutes with the gauge action and physical projection, and the restricted physical Hamiltonian $H_{\rm phys}=H|_{D(H)\cap\mathcal H_{\rm phys}}$ is self-adjoint on $D(H)\cap\mathcal H_{\rm phys}$. The restricted group has skew-adjoint infinitesimal generator $-iH_{\rm phys}/\hbar$ and self-adjoint Stone operator $-H_{\rm phys}/\hbar$, both on that same domain. This current mathematical carrier is draft with a complete conditional proof and a Step-1 ready record, not independent proof acceptance.

## Proof

**Given:** [A1], [L1], [F1]–[F3], and $\hbar>0$.

1.1 To check the weaker choice hypothesis in [L1], let $(X_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ be any sequence of nonempty sets. Apply [A1] to the family $\{X_n:n\in\mathbb N\}$ and obtain a choice function $g$ on that family; then $f(n):=g(X_n)$ belongs to $X_n$ for every $n$. Thus full AC supplies the Countable Choice input required by [F1]–[F3]. [A1, L1, given, construct]

1.2 The hypotheses in [F1] identify the adopted Hamiltonian, background range and maximal domain with the exact finite-graph data used by [F2] and [F3]; no continuum or spatial embedding data are needed for those mathematical suppliers. [F1, F2, F3, given]

1.3 For every vertex $x$, the allowed range $0\le b_x\le s$ lets us occupy exactly $b_x$ of its $s$ modes, including zero or all modes at the endpoints. Tensor the resulting normalized finite occupation vector with the Fourier basis vector having every link label $n_e=0$. Every link contribution to each Gauss multiplier then vanishes, including the cancelling outgoing and incoming terms of a self-loop; the matter term is $-(b_x-b_x)=0$. Thus $\gamma_x=0$ at each vertex, so [F2] places this nonzero vector in $\mathcal H_{\rm phys}$. [F1, F2, construct]

2.1 By [F3], $H$ is self-adjoint on exactly $D(H_0)$ and its unitary group preserves the physical projection. Restricting that group to the nonzero closed range $\mathcal H_{\rm phys}$ therefore gives the stated strongly continuous unitary group; [F3] gives its exact derivative domain and self-adjoint restricted Hamiltonian. The units in [F1] make $tH/\hbar$ dimensionless. [A1, F1, F3, step 1.2, step 1.3, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume the finite-graph model of
[[post-qft-compact-lattice-gauge-model]] and the Axiom of Choice. Write
$\mathcal U(t)=e^{-itH/\hbar}$ for the unitary group of
[[pthm-qft-lattice-gauge-existence]], and let
$\mathcal H_{\rm phys}=\bigcap_x\ker G_x$ be its nonzero physical sector.

For a bounded operator $O$ on $\mathcal H_{\rm kin}$, define its gauge charge
$q=(q_x)_{x\in V}\in\mathbb Z^V$ by
$$U(\alpha)OU(\alpha)^\dagger=e^{i\sum_x q_x\alpha_x}O \quad(\alpha\in\mathbb T^V).$$
For each normalized $\psi\in\mathcal H_{\rm phys}$,
$\langle\psi,O\psi\rangle=0$ when $q\ne0$. A finite product of bounded
gauge-charge eigenoperators has zero expectation whenever the sum of its
charge vectors is nonzero. If $O$ maps $D(G_x)$ into itself and
$[G_x,O]$ extends to a bounded operator, then
$\langle\psi,[G_x,O]\psi\rangle=0$. These statements also hold for
$O(t)=\mathcal U(t)^\dagger O\mathcal U(t)$; the finite-regulator evolution
preserves gauge charge and the domains $D(G_x)$.

For a fixed vertex $x$, distinct real insertion times $t_1,\ldots,t_n$ with
$n\ge1$, bounded operators $O_j$ that map $D(G_x)$ into itself, and bounded
commutators $[G_x,O_j]$, define ordinary time ordering by placing the factor
with larger time to the left. With
$O_j(t_j)=\mathcal U(t_j)^\dagger O_j\mathcal U(t_j)$ and
$G_x(t)=\mathcal U(t)^\dagger G_x\mathcal U(t)$, the following identity holds
as a distribution in $t$ between normalized physical/domain vectors:
$$\frac{d}{dt}\left\langle\psi,\mathcal T\!\left[G_x(t)\prod_{j=1}^nO_j(t_j)\right]\psi\right\rangle =\sum_{j=1}^n\delta(t-t_j) \left\langle\psi,\mathcal T\!\left([G_x,O_j(t_j)]\prod_{i\ne j}O_i(t_i)\right)\psi\right\rangle.$$
The products are evaluated on the stated common domains and $G_x$ is
bosonic, so no grading sign is inserted.

For a region $R\subseteq V$, define its boundary links by
$$\partial R=\{e\in E:\text{exactly one endpoint of }e\text{ lies in }R\},$$
with $\epsilon(e,R)=1$ for a link directed out of $R$ and $-1$ for a link
directed into $R$. On
$\mathcal D_R=\mathcal H_{\rm phys}\cap\bigcap_{e\in\partial R}D(E_e)$, put
$Q_R^{\rm lat}=\sum_{x\in R}(n_x-b_xI)$. If bounded $O$ preserves
$\mathcal H_{\rm phys}$, maps each boundary $D(E_e)$ into itself, and
$E_eO\phi=OE_e\phi$ for every $\phi\in D(E_e)$ and every $e\in\partial R$,
then $[Q_R^{\rm lat},O]\psi=0$ for every $\psi\in\mathcal D_R$. Consequently,
an operator that changes $Q_R^{\rm lat}$ by a fixed nonzero charge cannot
satisfy all these preservation and boundary-commutation hypotheses while
acting nontrivially on that domain.

There is also a separate conditional continuum implication; it does not assert
that a continuum representation exists. Let $\mathcal H_c$ be a Hilbert space
and $D\subseteq\mathcal H_c$ a common invariant dense domain. For real
$f,g_k\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$, let
$\rho(f),E_k(g_k):D\to D$ be linear assignments and put
$E(\mathbf g)=\sum_{k=1}^3E_k(g_k)$ for real
$\mathbf g=(g_1,g_2,g_3)\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$. Fix
$\varepsilon_0>0$ and assume
$$\rho(f)=-\varepsilon_0\sum_{k=1}^3E_k(\partial_k f) \quad(f\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)).$$
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^3$ be compact. Suppose bounded $O$ maps $D$ into
itself and $E(\mathbf g)O\psi=OE(\mathbf g)\psi$ for every $\psi\in D$ whenever
$\operatorname{supp}\mathbf g$ is disjoint from $K$. For integers
$R\ge R_0$, suppose real $\chi_R\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ equals $1$ on a
neighborhood of $K$, $\operatorname{supp}\nabla\chi_R$ is disjoint from $K$,
and, with $Q_R^{\rm cont}:=\rho(\chi_R)
=-\varepsilon_0E(\nabla\chi_R)$, there is $Q:D\to D$ such that
$Q_R^{\rm cont}\psi\to Q\psi$ and
$Q_R^{\rm cont}O\psi\to QO\psi$ for every $\psi\in D$. Then
$[Q,O]\psi=0$ on $D$. If also $[Q,O]\psi=qO\psi$ on $D$ for a fixed
$q\ne0$, boundedness of $O$ implies $O=0$ on $\mathcal H_c$. This clause is
conditional on the displayed common-domain, Gauss, locality and limit
hypotheses only.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The adopted finite-graph model, full AC, the nonzero physical
sector and its unitary evolution, the exact finite-regulator Ward suppliers,
and, separately, the continuum hypotheses in the Statement.

[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: every family of nonempty sets has a choice
function. It supplies the choice premise used by the finite-graph evolution
and Ward suppliers.

[F1] [[pthm-qft-lattice-gauge-existence]]: under the adopted fixed finite
model and full AC, $\mathcal H_{\rm phys}$ is nonzero and the exact
self-adjoint Hamiltonian generates a strongly continuous unitary group
preserving that sector. This is the preceding item on this page and is
conditional on its stated draft mathematical inputs.

[L1] [[lem-qft-lattice-ward-identities]]: for bounded gauge-charge operators,
physical-state expectations vanish at nonzero total charge; under the stated
$D(G_x)$ and bounded-commutator hypotheses the infinitesimal matrix element
vanishes; the exact evolution preserves charge and those domains. The current
carrier is draft with a complete conditional proof and a Step-1 ready record,
not independent proof acceptance.

[L2] [[lem-qft-lattice-ward-contact]]: for pairwise distinct times and
domain-preserving bounded insertions with bounded $G_x$ commutators, the
time-ordered contact identity holds distributionally; the current carrier is
a draft with a complete conditional proof and a Step-1 ready record.

[L3] [[lem-qft-qed-gauss-localization]]: on the finite graph, a bounded
physical-sector-preserving operator that preserves each boundary electric
domain and commutes with its electric operator there has zero regional-charge
commutator on the common physical/electric domain. Its separate continuum clause
requires exactly the common-domain, Gauss, locality and convergence assumptions
listed in the Statement. This current draft carrier has a complete conditional
proof and a Step-1 ready record.

## Proof

**Given:** [A1], [F1], [L1]–[L3], and the separate continuum assumptions in the
Statement.

1.1 By [F1], under the adopted model and full AC the physical sector is a
nonzero Hilbert subspace and $\mathcal U(t)$ is its exact unitary evolution.
Thus the physical vectors and time-evolved insertions in the finite clauses
are those of the declared regulator, not an assumed continuum state space.
[A1, F1, given]

1.2 For any normalized physical $\psi$ and gauge-charge eigenoperator with
$q\ne0$, the gauge transformations fix $\psi$ while multiplying the operator
by its charge character. Choosing a vertex $x$ with $q_x\ne0$ and
$\alpha_x=\pi/q_x$ makes that character $-1$, so its expectation must vanish.
For a finite product, inserting $U(\alpha)^\dagger U(\alpha)=I$ between
factors adds their charges; the same argument applies if their total charge
is nonzero. The exact gauge transformation, domain and evolution hypotheses
are those in [L1], so the finite selection and infinitesimal identities apply

$$M(Q)\ge\sum_{i=1}^N m_i.$$

## Statement

Let $\Omega\subseteq M$ be an open region of the prescribed background and let $K$ be a smooth Killing field on $\Omega$. For a massive force-postulate trajectory $x:I\to M$, parameterized by proper time on a nonempty open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ with $x(I)\subseteq\Omega$, constant $m>0$, $P=mU$, and $D_\tau P=f$, the scalar $g(K,P)$ obeys

$$\frac{d}{d\tau}g(K,P)=g(K,f).$$

Thus it is constant when the body is free ($f=0$). For a free null geodesic $y:J\to M$ on a nonempty open interval $J\subseteq\mathbb R$, with $y(J)\subseteq\Omega$, affine parameter $\lambda$, and tangent momentum $P=dy/d\lambda$, $g(K,P)$ is constant along $\lambda$ as well. If $K$ is a future unit timelike observer field along the applicable curve, then $-c\,g(K,P)$ has energy units and is the energy defined by that observer; for a general Killing field it is only a conserved scalar, not automatically an energy.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The smooth metric-compatible torsion-free connection, Killing field, force law, and null branch in the Statement.

[F1] A Killing field satisfies $\mathcal L_Kg=0$ ([[def-gr-killing-field]]).

[F2] Along a curve, $\frac{d}{d\tau}g(V,W)=g(D_\tau V,W)+g(V,D_\tau W)$ ([[lem-gr-parallel-transport-and-geodesic-speed]]).

[F3] On the massive branch $P=mU$ and $D_\tau P=f$ with $g(U,f)=0$ are the adopted constant-mass force assumptions ([[def-rpm-mechanical-momentum-and-observer-energy]], [[post-rpm-prescribed-force-law]]).

[F4] The null sector adopts independent einbein variation ([[post-rpm-null-test-particle-action]]); its nonzero future-null branch satisfies $P=T/e$ and $D_\lambda P=0$ ([[lem-rpm-einbein-variation-and-equivalence]]).

[F5] The Levi-Civita connection is metric-compatible and torsion-free; in a chart these properties give $\partial_cg_{ab}=\Gamma^d{}_{ca}g_{db}+\Gamma^d{}_{cb}g_{ad}$ and $\Gamma^d{}_{ab}=\Gamma^d{}_{ba}$ ([[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]], [[lem-gr-connection-conditions-in-chart-components]]).

[F6] A differentiable scalar function with zero derivative on an interval is constant ([[cor-zero-derivative-implies-constant]]).

## Proof

1.1 In any chart, differentiating the flow pullback that defines $\mathcal L_Kg$ gives $(\mathcal L_Kg)_{ab}=K^c\partial_cg_{ab}+g_{cb}\partial_aK^c+g_{ac}\partial_bK^c$: in the coordinate expression $(\Phi_t^*g)_{ab}=g_{cd}(\Phi_t(x))\partial_a\Phi_t^c\partial_b\Phi_t^d$, use $\Phi_t^c(x)=x^c+tK^c(x)+o(t)$ and $\partial_a\Phi_t^c=\delta_a^c+t\partial_aK^c+o(t)$. On the other hand, $K_b=g_{bc}K^c$ gives $\nabla_aK_b+\nabla_bK_a=\partial_a(g_{bc}K^c)+\partial_b(g_{ac}K^c)-2\Gamma^d{}_{ab}g_{dc}K^c$. Expanding and substituting [F5], the terms with $\Gamma^d{}_{ab}$ cancel by torsion-freeness, and the remaining metric-derivative terms become $K^c\partial_cg_{ab}$ by metric compatibility. Thus $\nabla_aK_b+\nabla_bK_a=(\mathcal L_Kg)_{ab}$ on this region, without an orientability hypothesis. Since $K$ is Killing by [F1], this symmetrized covariant derivative vanishes. Now metric compatibility [F2] gives $\frac{d}{d\tau}g(K,P)=g(D_\tau K,P)+g(K,D_\tau P)$. With $P=mU$, the first term is $m g(D_UK,U)=\tfrac m2(\nabla_aK_b+\nabla_bK_a)U^aU^b=0$. Substituting [F3] proves the forced balance $d g(K,P)/d\tau=g(K,f)$. [given, F1, F2, F3, F5, algebra]

2.1 If $f=0$, step 1.1 gives zero derivative, so [F6] makes the scalar constant on the connected parameter interval. On a free null curve, [F2] and [F4] give $d g(K,P)/d\lambda=g(D_PK,P)$; the same locally derived identity from step 1.1 with $X=Y=P$ makes this zero, hence the null scalar is constant. [step 1.1, F2, F4, F6, algebra]

3.1 If $K$ is a future unit observer, [F3] gives $E_K(P)=-c g(P,K)=-c g(K,P)$ by symmetry of $g$. With $P$ in kg m s$^{-1}$ and $c$ in m s$^{-1}$, this has units joules. For other Killing fields that observer definition does not apply, so the conserved quantity remains only a scalar. [F3, given] ∎

## Statement

Let a finite isolated collision have future-timelike total $Q$ of invariant mass $M>0$, and set $W:=Mc^2$. Suppose the complete outgoing list consists of exactly two legs, with recorded rest masses $a,b\ge0$; by the adopted balance postulate, their four-momenta must sum to $Q$. In a center-of-momentum frame with time-axis observer $n_Q$, a nonzero two-product state with $\mathbf p_a+\mathbf p_b=0$ exists exactly when

$$W\ge(a+b)c^2\quad\hbox{if }a,b>0,\qquad W>(a+b)c^2\quad\hbox{if }a=0\hbox{ or }b=0.$$

When it exists, there are $k\ge0$ and a unit vector $\mathbf e\in n_Q^\perp$ such that $\mathbf p_a=k\mathbf e$ and $\mathbf p_b=-k\mathbf e$. The energies and momentum magnitude are

$$E_a=\frac{W^2+(a^2-b^2)c^4}{2W},\qquad E_b=\frac{W^2+(b^2-a^2)c^4}{2W},\qquad k^2=\frac{[W^2-(a+b)^2c^4][W^2-(a-b)^2c^4]}{4W^2c^2}.$$

For $a,b>0$ at threshold, $k=0$ and the direction is immaterial. If a massless product is present, the strict threshold is required because a zero momentum would be the forbidden zero four-vector. These equations describe kinematic balance only. In SI units $a,b,M$ are kilograms, $W,E_a,E_b$ are joules, and $k$ is kilogram metres per second; the norm and dot product on $n_Q^\perp$ are induced by $\eta$.

## Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** A timelike total $Q$, a center-of-momentum observer $n_Q$, two specified nonnegative rest masses $a,b$, and the adopted finite collision-balance model.

[A1] [[post-rpm-isolated-collision-balance]]: a complete isolated event balances the finite incoming and outgoing four-momentum sums.

[F1] [[def-rpm-collision-objects]]: a massive final leg is future timelike with its recorded positive mass; a massless leg is a nonzero future-null vector with recorded mass zero.

[F2] [[pthm-rpm-system-mass-threshold]]: the total mass is $M>0$, the center-of-momentum energy is $W=Mc^2$, and any final list obeys the rest-mass threshold.

[F3] [[lem-sr-center-of-momentum-frame]]: for future-timelike $Q$, a center-of-momentum frame exists with $Q=(Mc,\mathbf0)$ and its time-axis observer is $n_Q=Q/(Mc)$.

[F4] [[def-rpm-mechanical-momentum-and-observer-energy]]: relative to a future unit observer, the energy and spatial momentum are the observer decomposition of the same four-vector.

[F5] For a massive leg of recorded mass $a>0$, [[def-rpm-collision-objects]] and [[def-rpm-mechanical-momentum-and-observer-energy]] give $P=aU$ with $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$, hence $\eta(P,P)=-a^2c^2$ by bilinearity; [[lem-sr-future-causal-sums-and-inertial-coordinate-criterion]] gives the future-cone coordinate criterion in the center-of-momentum frame.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** solve the two on-shell equations in the total rest frame and verify the converse construction.

1.1 In the center-of-momentum frame from [F3], $Q=(W/c)n_Q$ has zero total spatial momentum, so balance [A1] forces $\mathbf p_b=-\mathbf p_a$. Put $k:=|\mathbf p_a|\ge0$; if $k>0$, write $\mathbf p_a=k\mathbf e$ with $|\mathbf e|=1$ in the Euclidean rest space $n_Q^\perp$. The massive and null mass shells from [F1] and [F5] give $E_a^2=a^2c^4+c^2k^2$ and $E_b^2=b^2c^4+c^2k^2$, while the time component of balance is $E_a+E_b=W$ by [F2] and [F4]. [A1, F1, F2, F3, F4, F5]

2.1 Subtracting the shell equations and using $E_a+E_b=W>0$ gives $(E_a-E_b)W=(a^2-b^2)c^4$. Solving this and $E_a+E_b=W$ yields the stated $E_a,E_b$ formulas. Substituting the formula for $E_a$ into $c^2k^2=E_a^2-a^2c^4$ and factoring gives the stated expression for $k^2$. [step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Necessity of $W\ge(a+b)c^2$ follows from [F2]. Conversely, under this bound the second factor in $k^2$ is nonnegative because $W\ge(a+b)c^2\ge|a-b|c^2$. Also $E_a-ac^2=((W-ac^2)^2-b^2c^4)/(2W)\ge0$ and symmetrically $E_b-bc^2\ge0$, so both energies are future-directed. If $a,b>0$, equality at $W=(a+b)c^2$ gives $k=0$ and two valid massive legs. If either mass is zero, that equality gives zero momentum and zero energy for that leg, which is not an admissible nonzero null vector; hence the strict bound is necessary and sufficient in that case. [F1, F2, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 Under the stated admissible bound, choose any unit vector $\mathbf e\in n_Q^\perp$ (this rest space is three-dimensional by [F3]) and define $P_a=(E_a/c)n_Q+k\mathbf e$, $P_b=(E_b/c)n_Q-k\mathbf e$. Their spatial sum is zero and their energies sum to $W$, so $P_a+P_b=(W/c)n_Q=Q$. Their orthogonal decompositions and the formulas for $E_a,E_b,k$ give $\eta(P_a,P_a)=-a^2c^2$ and $\eta(P_b,P_b)=-b^2c^2$; the energies are positive, and any zero-mass leg has $k>0$, so both vectors are nonzero future causal by the cone criterion in [F5]. Thus the constructed pair satisfies the balance and both mass shells. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Consider a two-product elastic channel in a finite isolated collision: the complete incoming and outgoing lists each have exactly two legs, their recorded rest masses agree pairwise, the total four-momentum is timelike, and the balance postulate is adopted. In the center-of-momentum frame, let the incoming momenta be $k\mathbf e_{\rm in}$ and $-k\mathbf e_{\rm in}$ in the spatial rest space $n_Q^\perp$, where $k\ge0$ is fixed by [[pthm-rpm-two-body-com-kinematics]]. Every admissible outgoing pair has the same momentum magnitude $k$. If $k>0$, any unit vector $\mathbf e_{\rm out}\in n_Q^\perp$ gives an on-shell outgoing pair $k\mathbf e_{\rm out},-k\mathbf e_{\rm out}$ with the same total four-momentum; thus kinematics alone leaves the full direction sphere available. If $k=0$, both products are at rest and the direction is undefined. No isotropic or uniform distribution of directions follows.

## Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** A mass-specified isolated event with two incoming and two outgoing legs, equal paired masses, a timelike total $Q$, and the center-of-momentum frame of $Q$.

[A1] [[post-rpm-isolated-collision-balance]]: the complete isolated collision balances the incoming and outgoing totals.

[F1] [[def-rpm-collision-objects]]: a two-leg event has finite on-shell massive or nonzero null legs with recorded masses.

[F2] [[pthm-rpm-two-body-com-kinematics]]: for fixed $W$ and product masses, the on-shell two-body momentum magnitude is the displayed unique $k$, and every unit rest-space direction yields a balanced pair when the massless endpoint condition is met.

[F3] [[def-rpm-mechanical-momentum-and-observer-energy]]: the spatial momentum is the projection of the same four-momentum into the observer rest space.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** compare the unique two-body shell magnitude before and after.

1.1 Apply [F2] to the incoming pair with masses $a,b$ and total rest energy $W=Mc^2$. It has a unique magnitude $k$ determined by $W,a,b$. The outgoing pair has the same two masses by the elastic hypothesis and the same total by [A1], so [F2] gives the same $W$ and the same magnitude $k$. [A1, F1, F2]

2.1 If $k>0$, let $\mathbf e_{\rm out}$ be any unit vector in $n_Q^\perp$ and use [F2] to construct the two outgoing momenta with spatial parts $\pm k\mathbf e_{\rm out}$ and the corresponding energies. They satisfy both mass shells and sum to $Q$. If $k=0$, the spatial parts vanish, so no direction is defined. The free kinematic parameter supplies no probability measure or scattering dynamics, hence it entails no isotropic law. [F2, F3, step 1.1] ∎

## Statement

For a massive body with constant $m>0$, $P=mU$, $g(U,U)=-c^2$, and the force law of [[post-rpm-prescribed-force-law]],

$$g(P,P)=-m^2c^2.$$

For every observer $n$ at the event, the energy and spatial momentum defined in [[def-rpm-mechanical-momentum-and-observer-energy]] satisfy

$$E_n(P)^2=m^2c^4+c^2g(q_n(P),q_n(P)),\qquad E_n(P)>0.$$

For a nonzero future-null $P$, $E_n(P)=c\sqrt{g(q_n(P),q_n(P))}$. In a flat inertial frame $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ with $n=e_0$ and inertial chart $x^0=ct$ from [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], let $E=E_n(P)$, let $\mathbf p$ be the spatial coordinates of $q_n(P)$ in $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$, set $\mathbf v=d\mathbf x/dt$, and define $\mathbf F=d\mathbf p/dt$. Then $dE/dt=\mathbf F\cdot\mathbf v$ under the constant-mass force hypotheses. If $m(\tau)>0$ is $C^1$, $U$ is $C^1$ with $g(U,U)=-c^2$, and $P=m(\tau)U$, then the kinematic identity $g(U,D_\tau P)=-c^2\dot m$ holds; it specifies no variable-mass law.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A future unit timelike tangent $U$, constant $m>0$ on the massive branch, an observer $n$, and the force assumptions of the Statement.

[F1] The prescribed force is orthogonal to $U$ and the local IVP preserves $g(U,U)=-c^2$ ([[post-rpm-prescribed-force-law]], [[lem-rpm-shell-tangent-force-ivp]]).

[F2] For an observer, $q_n(P)=P+g(P,n)n$ and $g(q_n(P),q_n(P))=g(P,P)+g(P,n)^2$ ([[def-rpm-mechanical-momentum-and-observer-energy]], [[lem-gr-observer-projection-decomposition]]).

[F3] Pairing a future timelike vector with a future observer is strictly negative ([[lem-gr-observer-pairing-with-future-causal-vectors]]).

[F4] In a flat inertial chart with constant mass, the four-force work identity gives $dE/dt=\mathbf F\cdot\mathbf v$ ([[lem-sr-four-force-and-work-energy-identities]]).

[F5] Along a curve, $\frac{d}{d\tau}g(V,W)=g(D_\tau V,W)+g(V,D_\tau W)$ ([[lem-gr-parallel-transport-and-geodesic-speed]]).

## Proof

1.1 From $P=mU$ and $g(U,U)=-c^2$, $g(P,P)=m^2g(U,U)=-m^2c^2$. Write $a=-g(P,n)$ and $q=q_n(P)$; then $P=a n+q$, $g(q,n)=0$, and [F2] gives $g(q,q)=g(P,P)+g(P,n)^2$. Since $E_n=ca$, rearrangement yields $E_n^2=m^2c^4+c^2g(q,q)$. [given, F2, algebra]

1.2 The vectors $P$ and $n$ are future timelike, so [F3] gives $g(P,n)<0$ and therefore $E_n=-cg(P,n)>0$. For null $P$, since $g(P,P)=0$, [F2] yields $g(q,q)=g(P,n)^2$, and positivity selects $E_n=c\sqrt{g(q,q)}$. [F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 Under the flat inertial constant-mass hypotheses, [F1] identifies the prescribed force with the derivative of the mechanical momentum, and [F4] supplies the coordinate work relation. If $P=m(\tau)U$, differentiating $g(U,U)=-c^2$ using metric compatibility gives $g(U,D_\tau U)=0$; hence $g(U,D_\tau P)=\dot m\,g(U,U)+m g(U,D_\tau U)=-c^2\dot m$. This last identity imposes no dynamics for $m$. [given, F1, F4, F5, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Fix a reference speed $c_*>0$, mass $m>0$, charge $q\in\mathbb R$, cutoff $0<\delta<1$, finite time $T>0$, an open time interval $I\supseteq[0,T]$, and an open spatial region $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$. In a fixed inertial chart with $x^0=ct$, let $\mathbf E,\mathbf B:I\times\Omega\to\mathbb R^3$ be prescribed jointly $C^1$ fields in SI units, with $\mathbf E$ in volts per metre and $\mathbf B$ in teslas. The same fields, mass, and charge are held fixed in the following formal family of model equations indexed by $c>0$; no Maxwell equations or empirical premise are added.

Choose reference scales $L_*>0$ metres and $P_*>0$ kilogram metres per second and define the dimensionless state norm

$$\|(x,p)\|_*:=\frac{|x|}{L_*}+\frac{|p|}{P_*}.$$

Let $\pi_x:\Omega\times\mathbb R^3\to\Omega$ be the spatial projection $\pi_x(x,p):=x$, and let $K\ne\varnothing$ be a compact convex subset of $\Omega\times\mathbb R^3$. With $|\cdot|$ the Euclidean norm, put $P_{\max}:=\sup_{(x,p)\in K}|p|$, $E_{\max}:=\sup_{(t,x)\in[0,T]\times\pi_xK}|\mathbf E(t,x)|$, and $B_{\max}:=\sup_{(t,x)\in[0,T]\times\pi_xK}|\mathbf B(t,x)|$. These field suprema are finite by the $C^1$ hypothesis on a compact cylinder. Set

$$B_*:=\frac{P_{\max}}{mL_*}+\frac{|q|}{P_*}\left(E_{\max}+\frac{P_{\max}B_{\max}}m\right).$$

For $c>0$ with $c\ge P_{\max}/(m\delta)$, define the momentum-to-velocity map

$$V_c(p):=\frac{p}{m\sqrt{1+|p|^2/(m^2c^2)}}.$$

This is the velocity obtained from the massive mass shell and inverse momentum formula of [[pthm-rpm-inverse-momentum-and-work]]. Define the relativistic and Newtonian vector fields on $[0,T]\times K$ by

$$G_c(t,x,p):=\bigl(V_c(p),\,q[\mathbf E(t,x)+V_c(p)\times\mathbf B(t,x)]\bigr),\qquad G_N(t,x,p):=\bigl(p/m,\,q[\mathbf E(t,x)+(p/m)\times\mathbf B(t,x)]\bigr).$$

Suppose there is $L\ge0$, with units $\mathrm{s}^{-1}$, such that for all $t\in[0,T]$ and states $\zeta,\widetilde\zeta\in K$,

$$\|G_N(t,\zeta)-G_N(t,\widetilde\zeta)\|_*\le L\|\zeta-\widetilde\zeta\|_*.$$

For every $c>0$ in the family, $G_c$ and $G_N$ are bounded by $B_*$ in $\|\cdot\|_*$ on $[0,T]\times K$, since $|V_c(p)|\le P_{\max}/m$. For each $c>0$ with $c\ge P_{\max}/(m\delta)$, let $J\subseteq I$ be an open interval containing $[0,T]$ and let $x_c\in C^2(J,\Omega)$ satisfy $|\dot x_c(t)|<c$. Define the coordinate velocity $v_c(t):=\dot x_c(t)$ and Lorentz factor $\gamma_c(t):=(1-|v_c(t)|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$. The curve $X_c(t)=(ct,x_c(t))$ is a future-timelike massive worldline with proper time $d\tau/dt=\sqrt{1-|v_c(t)|^2/c^2}$ and four-velocity $U_c=\gamma_c(c,v_c)$; its spatial momentum is $p_c=m\gamma_c v_c$. Assume $X_c$ satisfies the adopted covariant Lorentz coupling in the prescribed field. Define $z_c(t):=(x_c(t),p_c(t))$. Let $(x_N,p_N)$ be a $C^1$ solution on $[0,T]$ of $\dot z=G_N(t,z)$ and set $z_N(t):=(x_N(t),p_N(t))$. Require $z_c(0)=z_N(0)$ and both coordinate-state trajectories to remain in $K$. Then the relativistic coordinates satisfy $\dot z_c=G_c(t,z_c)$, and, with $\epsilon_c:=(c_*/c)^2$ and

$$C_*:=\frac{P_{\max}^3}{2m^3c_*^2}\left(\frac1{L_*}+\frac{|q|B_{\max}}{P_*}\right),$$

one has

$$\sup_{0\le t\le T}\|(x_c(t),p_c(t))-(x_N(t),p_N(t))\|_*\le C_*\epsilon_c T e^{LT}.$$

Here $C_*$ has units $\mathrm{s}^{-1}$. Consequently the state difference is $O(c^{-2})$ on this fixed interval as $c\to\infty$, provided the common containment and Lipschitz hypotheses hold for the family.

For every $t\in[0,T]$, the relativistic speed satisfies $|v_c(t)|/c\le\delta$. If $\mathcal E_c(t):=\sqrt{m^2c^4+c^2|p_c(t)|^2}$ is the particle energy from the same mass shell, then [[lem-rpm-low-speed-remainders]] also gives

$$|p_c-mv_c|\le\frac{m|v_c|^3}{2c^2(1-\delta^2)^{3/2}},\qquad 0\le\mathcal E_c-mc^2-\frac12m|v_c|^2\le\frac{3m|v_c|^4}{8c^2(1-\delta^2)^{5/2}}.$$

The limit is a formal comparison between model equations; it does not state that the SI value of $c$ varies in nature.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The prescribed field maps and their regularity and units, $m>0$, constant $q$, the reference scales, compact convex state set, $P_{\max}$, $B_{\max}$, Lipschitz constant $L$, and for each stated $c$ an existing future-timelike $C^2$ worldline satisfying the adopted coupling together with an existing Newtonian comparison solution, with common initial state and compact containment.

[A1] The adopted flat massive-particle model uses constant mass $m>0$, momentum $P=mU$, and the fixed flat inertial-frame conventions; it is a physical assumption, not an empirical finding ([[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]], [[post-em-minkowski-physical-model]]).

[A2] The prescribed external Lorentz coupling adopts $m\,dU/d\tau=q\Phi(U)$ with constant charge $q$, positive external rest mass, and no self-field ([[post-em-lorentz-coupling]]).

[F1] The supplier fields are $\mathbf E_s,\mathbf B_s:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$, of class $C^1$, with units V m$^{-1}$ and T ([[def-em-fields]], [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-em-si-conventions]]). The Statement's time-first notation means $\mathbf E(t,x):=\mathbf E_s(x,t)$ and $\mathbf B(t,x):=\mathbf B_s(x,t)$; it is an argument swap, not a different field. Since $\Omega$ is open, $\mathcal U:=\Omega\times\mathbb R^3$ is an open state domain in $\mathbb R^6$. The formulas for $G_c,G_N$ in the Statement define $C^1$ maps on $[0,T]\times\mathcal U$, whose restrictions are the fields used on $[0,T]\times K$; thus $K$ may be compact without being open. In SI, $c,c_*$ are m s$^{-1}$, $m$ is kg, $q$ is C, $t,T$ are seconds, $x,L_*$ are metres, $p,P_*$ are kg m s$^{-1}$, and particle energy is J ([[def-em-si-conventions]], [[def-em-sources]], [[def-em-lab-geometry]]). Thus $\|\cdot\|_*$ and $\epsilon_c$ are dimensionless; $B_*,L,C_*$ have units s$^{-1}$, while $E_{\max}$ and $B_{\max}$ have units V m$^{-1}$ and T. The remaining SI component dictionary is $F^{0i}=E_i/c$, $F^{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$, $x^0=ct$ ([[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]], [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]]).

[L1] Under [A1]–[A2] and the $C^1$ prescribed-field hypotheses, the published EM result gives $dp/dt=q(\mathbf E+v\times\mathbf B)$ with $p=m\gamma v$ on every $C^2$ worldline; it excludes self-field and radiation reaction ([[pthm-em-relativistic-lorentz-force]]).

[L2] For the constant-mass massive inertial branch, $p=m\gamma v$, $\mathcal E=\gamma mc^2$, $\mathcal E^2=m^2c^4+c^2|p|^2$, and $v=c^2p/\mathcal E$; the current in-run supplier has draft status and its exact statement is used conditionally ([[pthm-rpm-inverse-momentum-and-work]]).

[L3] For $|v|/c\le\delta<1$, the exact pointwise momentum and energy remainder inequalities of [[lem-rpm-low-speed-remainders]] hold.

[F4] Vector-valued differentiation and integration are componentwise; a continuous $\mathbb R^6$-valued function on a compact interval has integrable components, and for a $C^1$ curve $z$ its derivative integrates to $z(t)-z(0)$ ([[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]], [[thm-componentwise-limits-and-continuity]], [[thm-continuous-implies-integrable]], [[cor-vector-valued-ftc-and-lipschitz-bound]]). For each integrable $h:[0,t]\to\mathbb R^3$, $\|\int_0^t h(s)\,ds\|_2\le\int_0^t\|h(s)\|_2\,ds$ ([[thm-norm-inequality-for-the-vector-valued-integral]]).

[F5] If continuous $u,a,b$ on $[0,T]$ satisfy $u,b\ge0$, $u(t)\le a(t)+\int_0^t b(s)u(s)\,ds$, and $a$ is nondecreasing, then $u(t)\le a(t)\exp(\int_0^t b(s)\,ds)$ ([[thm-gronwall-integral-inequality]]).

[F2] For $u\ge0$, $h(u)=1-(1+u)^{-1/2}$ satisfies $h(0)=0$ and $h'(u)=\frac12(1+u)^{-3/2}$ by the real-power derivative and chain rule; the mean value theorem applies to $h$ on every $[0,u]$ ([[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]], [[thm-chain-rule]], [[cor-mean-value-theorem]]).

[F3] In the Euclidean oriented space $\mathbb R^3$, the cross product is the alternating bilinear operation with components $(a_2b_3-a_3b_2,a_3b_1-a_1b_3,a_1b_2-a_2b_1)$ ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** invert the relativistic mass shell, bound the relativistic-to-Newtonian vector-field difference uniformly, then prove the weighted-norm comparison by blockwise integration and Gronwall.

1.1 The stated future-timelike $C^2$ worldline has four-velocity $U_c=\gamma_c(c,\dot x_c)$ and mechanical momentum $p_c=m\gamma_c\dot x_c$. By [L1], its spatial momentum obeys $\dot p_c=q[\mathbf E(t,x_c)+\dot x_c\times\mathbf B(t,x_c)]$. By [L2], $\mathcal E_c=c\sqrt{m^2c^2+|p_c|^2}$ and $\dot x_c=c^2p_c/\mathcal E_c=p_c/[m\sqrt{1+|p_c|^2/(m^2c^2)}]=V_c(p_c)$. Thus the relativistic worldline coordinates satisfy $\dot z_c=G_c(t,z_c)$, while $z_N$ satisfies the declared Newtonian comparison equation by hypothesis. [given, A1, A2, F1, L1, L2, algebra]

1.2 Put $u=|p|^2/(m^2c^2)\ge0$ and $h(u)=1-(1+u)^{-1/2}$. By [F2], $h(0)=0$ and $h'(s)=\frac12(1+s)^{-3/2}\le\frac12$ for $s\ge0$; if $u>0$, the mean value theorem gives $0\le h(u)\le u/2$, and for $u=0$ the same holds by equality. Hence, for every $(x,p)\in K$, $|V_c(p)-p/m|=(|p|/m)h(u)\le P_{\max}^3/(2m^3c^2)$. Expanding the component definition in [F3] gives $|a\times b|^2=|a|^2|b|^2-(a\cdot b)^2\le|a|^2|b|^2$, so $\|G_c(t,x,p)-G_N(t,x,p)\|_* = |V_c-p/m|/L_*+|q|\,|(V_c-p/m)\times\mathbf B(t,x)|/P_*\le\frac{P_{\max}^3}{2m^3c^2}\left(\frac1{L_*}+\frac{|q|B_{\max}}{P_*}\right)=C_*\epsilon_c$. [given, L2, F2, F3, algebra]

1.3 Since $x_c$ is $C^2$, its speed stays strictly below $c$, and the mass-shell map is smooth, $p_c$ and $z_c$ are $C^1$; $z_N$ is $C^1$ by hypothesis. Let $H(s)=(H_x(s),H_p(s)):=G_c(s,z_c(s))-G_N(s,z_N(s))$, where each block is in $\mathbb R^3$. The fields on the open state domain and the solution curves are continuous, so $H$ has integrable components. By [F4], the vector-valued fundamental theorem gives $$z_c(t)-z_N(t)=z_c(0)-z_N(0)+\int_0^tH(s)\,ds.$$ Applying the Euclidean integral norm inequality of [F4] separately to the two blocks yields $$\Bigl\|\int_0^tH(s)\,ds\Bigr\|_*:=\frac{\bigl|\int_0^tH_x(s)\,ds\bigr|}{L_*}+\frac{\bigl|\int_0^tH_p(s)\,ds\bigr|}{P_*}\le\int_0^t\left(\frac{|H_x(s)|}{L_*}+\frac{|H_p(s)|}{P_*}\right)ds=\int_0^t\|H(s)\|_*\,ds.$$ For $t=0$ the same inequality holds with both sides zero. [given, F4, algebra]

2.1 Since $|V_c(p)|\le |p|/m\le P_{\max}/m$ and $|p|/m\le P_{\max}/m$ on $K$, the definitions of $G_c,G_N$, the cross-product bound proved in step 1.2, and the field suprema give $\|G_c(t,x,p)\|_*,\|G_N(t,x,p)\|_*\le B_*$. This proves the stated uniform field bound; stability will follow from the weighted-norm argument below. [given, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

2.2 Splitting $H(s)$ by adding and subtracting $G_N(s,z_c(s))$, the triangle inequality, step 1.2, and the assumed $L$-Lipschitz bound for $G_N$ on $K$ give $$d(t):=\|z_c(t)-z_N(t)\|_*\le d(0)+C_*\epsilon_c t+L\int_0^t d(s)\,ds.$$ The norm and Lipschitz constant here are exactly the weighted ones in the Statement; the estimate follows from the blockwise inequality of step 1.3, without applying the Euclidean comparison lemma to this norm. [given, step 1.2, step 1.3, algebra]

3.1 Set $a(t)=d(0)+C_*\epsilon_c t$ and $b(t)=L$. These functions are continuous, $a$ is nondecreasing and $b,d\ge0$, so [F5] gives $d(t)\le(d(0)+C_*\epsilon_c t)e^{Lt}$. The initial states agree, hence $d(0)=0$, and $t\le T$ gives $\sup_{0\le t\le T}d(t)\le C_*\epsilon_c T e^{LT}$. Since $\epsilon_c=c_*^2/c^2$ and the other quantities are fixed, this is $O(c^{-2})$ on the specified interval. [given, step 2.2, F5, algebra]

4.1 The inversion formula and $|p_c|\le P_{\max}$ imply $|\dot x_c|=|V_c(p_c)|\le P_{\max}/m$ and hence $|\dot x_c|/c\le P_{\max}/(mc)\le\delta$. Apply [L3] pointwise to the worldline speed $\dot x_c$ to obtain the two stated kinetic remainders. This only adds kinematic estimates; it does not derive a trajectory comparison from them. [given, step 1.1, L2, L3, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

The field and vector-field estimates are in a named inertial chart and use a formal model parameter $c$. Electric and magnetic fields are prescribed and held fixed, not solved self-consistently as $c$ varies. The common-interval solution and compact-containment assumptions are essential: neither bounded field values alone nor the pointwise low-speed estimates establish finite-time trajectory convergence.

## Statement

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold and let $m,c>0$. Let $\mathcal V\subset TM$ be an open set of future timelike vectors, and let $f$ be a smooth vector field along the bundle projection $\mathcal V\to M$, with $f(p,V)\in T_pM$. For the named massive test body, adopt the constant-mass force model of [[post-rpm-prescribed-force-law]]: $P=mU$, $g(U,U)=-c^2$, $D_\tau P=f(x,U)$, and $g(U,f(x,U))=0$. If $\tau$ is measured in seconds, then $P$ has SI units kilogram metres per second and $f$ has units newtons.

Fix an initial proper-time value $\tau_0\in\mathbb R$. For each initial datum $(p_0,U_0)\in\mathcal V$ with $g_{p_0}(U_0,U_0)=-c^2$, there is a unique local $C^2$ future-timelike worldline $x:J\to M$ on an open interval $J\ni\tau_0$, with $C^1$ tangent $U=dx/d\tau$, $x(\tau_0)=p_0$, and $U(\tau_0)=U_0$, satisfying the adopted equation. It remains on the future unit timelike shell and has a unique maximal solution on an open interval containing $\tau_0$. In any chart-state domain where the coordinate force vector field is smooth, if a finite endpoint is approached while the state remains in a compact subset of that domain, the solution extends past the endpoint. No global lifetime or spacetime completeness is asserted.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The prescribed smooth spacetime and force field, $m,c>0$, a specified initial proper-time value $\tau_0$, initial position $p_0$, future unit timelike initial velocity $U_0$, and the equalities $x(\tau_0)=p_0$, $U(\tau_0)=U_0$, and the adopted constant-mass force model.

[A1] The physical model is an optional adoption for a named massive test body with constant primitive $m>0$: on an open neighborhood of the future unit timelike shell it specifies a smooth force $f$, the equation $D_\tau P=f(x,U)$ with $P=mU$, and the compatibility condition $g(U,f(x,U))=0$ ([[post-rpm-prescribed-force-law]]). This is not a universal force principle; that postulate is a current in-run draft and is used here at its inspected statement.

[F1] The RPP background is a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, and massive worldlines are future timelike curves with a specified parameter; observer, congruence, adapted chart and tetrad are distinct objects ([[def-rpm-spacetime-observer-and-worldline]]).

[F2] In the adopted massive sector, the mechanical momentum is $P=mU$ for constant $m>0$ and $g(U,U)=-c^2$ ([[def-rpm-mechanical-momentum-and-observer-energy]]).

[L1] For a smooth force on an open future-timelike velocity domain with $g(U,f)=0$, the system $dx/ds=U$, $D_sU=f(x,U)/m$ has a unique local solution, preserves $g(U,U)=-c^2$ and future direction, and has a unique maximal open interval ([[lem-rpm-shell-tangent-force-ivp]]). The actual supplier is a draft from in-run batch 22, so the use here is conditional on its inspected interface and proof status.

[L2] A smooth solution of that shell-force equation which remains in a compact subset of its open chart-state domain cannot have a finite maximal endpoint ([[lem-rpm-shell-force-ivp]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** identify the adopted force equation with the shell-tangent ODE and apply its local and continuation results.

1.1 The prescribed smooth background and future timelike worldline use the conventions of [F1]. Since $m$ is constant, [F2] gives $D_\tau P=mD_\tau U$. Substituting [A1] yields $D_\tau U=f(x,U)/m$, with the force smooth on the open velocity domain and orthogonal to $U$. These are exactly the hypotheses of [L1], so apply [L1] with $s_0=\tau_0$ and $s=\tau$, so for each stated initial datum there is a unique local solution with $x(\tau_0)=p_0$ and $U(\tau_0)=U_0$; [L1] also proves preservation of the future unit timelike shell. [given, A1, F1, F2, L1, algebra]

2.1 The unique local solutions patch by uniqueness to the maximal open-interval solution supplied by [L1]. At either finite endpoint, if the coordinate state remained in a compact subset of a chart-state domain on which the force vector field is smooth, [L2] would extend that solution, contradicting maximality. Therefore every finite maximal endpoint leaves every such compact subset. [step 1.1, L1, L2] ∎

## Remarks

This is a model deduction conditional on the separately adopted force law. Orthogonality is the compatibility condition for constant-mass shell preservation; it does not select a physical interaction. The result does not prove that the model describes a measured body.

## Statement

Let $P_1,P_2$ be two nonzero future-null incoming momenta in a finite collision configuration, and let $n$ be the future unit observer of a named inertial laboratory frame. Define $E_i:=E_n(P_i)>0$, $\mathbf p_i:=q_n(P_i)$, and equip $n^\perp$ with the induced Euclidean inner product $\langle u,v\rangle_n:=\eta(u,v)$ and norm $|u|_n:=\sqrt{\langle u,u\rangle_n}$. Let $\theta\in[0,\pi]$ be their spatial angle, $\cos\theta=\langle\mathbf p_1,\mathbf p_2\rangle_n/(|\mathbf p_1|_n|\mathbf p_2|_n)$. For $Q:=P_1+P_2$ and $\sigma:=-c^2\eta(Q,Q)$,

$$\sigma=2E_1E_2(1-\cos\theta),\qquad M(Q)=\frac{\sqrt{\sigma}}{c^2}.$$

The total $Q$ is null exactly when $\theta=0$ (the two incoming vectors lie on one future null ray); it is timelike for $\theta>0$. In particular, for head-on momenta $\theta=\pi$, $M(Q)=2\sqrt{E_1E_2}/c^2$; if $E_1=E_2=E$, this is $2E/c^2$. The angle and the two energies depend on the named observer, while $\sigma$ and $M(Q)$ are invariant.

In SI units $E_1,E_2$ are joules, $\sigma$ is joules squared, and $M(Q)$ is kilograms; $\theta$ is dimensionless.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Two nonzero future-null incoming momenta, a future unit laboratory observer, and the finite collision-data conventions.

[F1] [[def-rpm-collision-objects]]: each null leg is a nonzero future-null vector; its momentum scale is specified independently of proper time.

[F2] [[def-rpm-mechanical-momentum-and-observer-energy]]: $E_n(P)=-c\eta(P,n)$, $q_n(P)=P+\eta(P,n)n$, and the observer rest space has its Euclidean inner product.

[F3] [[def-sr-total-four-momentum-and-invariant-mass]]: the total four-momentum is the finite vector sum; its invariant mass is $M(Q)=\sqrt{-\eta(Q,Q)}/c$ when $Q$ is future timelike, and $M(Q)=0$ when $Q$ is future null, with no rest frame in the null case.

Fix a positive constant reference density $f_{\rm ref}$ with the same units as $f$, and put $\ell(r,v,t)=\log(f(r,v,t)/f_{\rm ref})$. For each $t\in I$, assume $f$, $f|v|^2$, and $f|\ell|$ are integrable over $\Omega\times\mathbb R^d$. For every compact interval $I_0\subset I$, assume there is a nonnegative $G_{I_0}\in L^1(\Omega\times\mathbb R^d,dr\,dv)$ such that $|(1+\ell)\partial_t f|\le G_{I_0}$ almost everywhere for every $t\in I_0$. For each $t\in I$, assume $r\mapsto\int_{Q_{\rm el}}|(A-B)(\ell(r,v,t)+\ell(r,w,t)-\ell(r,v',t)-\ell(r,w',t))|\,d\nu$ is measurable and belongs to $L^1(\Omega,dr)$. Let $Q$ and the symmetric collision measure $\nu$ satisfy the weak identity in [[def-tdmath-elastic-collision-kernel]] for tests $1$ and $\ell(r,\cdot,t)$ at each $(r,t)$, with absolute convergence, and suppose
$$\partial_t f+v\cdot\nabla_r f=Q(f).$$
Then for $H[f](t)=\int_\Omega\int_{\mathbb R^d}f\ell\,dv\,dr$,
$$\frac{d}{dt}H[f](t)=-\frac14\int_\Omega\int_{Q_{\rm el}}(A-B)\log(A/B)\,d\nu\,dr\le0.$$
The integrand is nonnegative because $\log$ is strictly increasing. Equality in the entropy-production integral holds exactly when $A=B$ for $\nu$-almost every collision at almost every $r$. Under the additional assumptions that $\nu$ is locally finite, has full support on $Q_{\rm el}$, and $f$ is positive and $C^2$ in $v$, this balance implies for almost every $r$ that
$$\log(f(r,v,t)/f_{\rm ref})=\alpha(r,t)+b(r,t)\cdot v+\frac{\lambda(r,t)}2|v|^2.$$
If $f(r,\cdot,t)$ is integrable over $\mathbb R^d$, then $\lambda(r,t)<0$, so its velocity profile is Maxwellian. Conversely, every profile of this form has zero collision entropy production. The weak collision identity is an explicit model hypothesis; this is not a derivation from reversible many-particle mechanics or a PDE existence theorem.

Then $F_{\mathrm{stat}}:=-k_{\mathrm B}T\log Z=\bar E_\beta-TS_\beta$ for $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$. A lower bound on the energies alone does not supply the summable envelope or finite partition function.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A specified countable energy list, a positive finite canonical partition sum on $J_\beta$, and the local summable second-moment envelope.

## Statement

For every fixed $\beta>0$, the sequence $p_L(\beta)$ of [[def-tdmath-bounded-finite-range-lattice]] has a finite limit as $L\to\infty$. If another finite-volume energy $\widetilde H_L$ on the same configurations satisfies $\sup_s|\widetilde H_L(s)-H_L(s)|\le C_bL^{d-1}$ for a constant $C_b$ independent of $L$, define $\widetilde Z_L(\beta):=\sum_{s\in\mathcal A^{\Lambda_L}}e^{-\beta\widetilde H_L(s)}$ and $\widetilde p_L(\beta):=L^{-d}\log\widetilde Z_L(\beta)$. Then $\widetilde p_L$ has the same limit. The result covers finite-alphabet, bounded, translation-invariant finite-range interactions on cubic boxes; it asserts no continuum-particle or long-range limit.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** As stated in the item.

[A1] The dimension, alphabet, shapes, bounded interaction functions, free-boundary energies, and $\beta>0$ are exactly as in [[def-tdmath-bounded-finite-range-lattice]].

[F1] [[def-tdmath-bounded-finite-range-lattice]]: the alphabet has $q$ states per site, the (possibly empty) interaction list is finite, each term is bounded, and $Z_L$ is the finite partition sum.

[F3] [[thm-division-algorithm-in-z]]: for positive integer $\ell$ and integer $L\ge0$, write $L=k\ell+r$ with integer $k$ and remainder $0\le r<\ell$.

[F2] [[def-natural-logarithm]] and [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]]: $\log$ is increasing and converts products to sums.

## Proof

**Given:** The bounded finite-range lattice data, $\beta>0$, and (for the boundary comparison clause) the uniform $C_bL^{d-1}$ energy bound.

1.1 Write $V=L^d$ and $J_0=\sum_a\|\Phi_a\|_\infty$. Each configuration satisfies $|H_L(s)|\le J_0V$, so $q^Ve^{-\beta J_0V}\le Z_L\le q^Ve^{\beta J_0V}$. Hence $p_L$ is bounded above and below uniformly in $L$. [A1, F1, F2]

1.2 Fix an integer block length $\ell>2R$ and write $L=k\ell+r$ with $0\le r<\ell$ using [F3]. If $k<0$, then $L=k\ell+r\le-\ell+r<0$, contrary to $L\ge0$, so $k\ge0$. For the limiting estimate take $L\ge\ell$, hence $k\ge1$. Partition $\Lambda_L$ into $k^d$ disjoint $\ell$-cubes and an outer remainder. Form $H_{L,\ell}^{\rm cut}$ by retaining only interactions whose entire support lies in one full cube and assigning zero energy to remainder sites. For a fixed shape, every eligible anchor lies in $[1-R,L+R]^d$. If its support crosses an internal block seam, its coordinate normal to that seam lies in at most $2R+1$ integer positions; the other coordinates have at most $(L+2R)^{d-1}$ choices. If it is not in such a seam strip but the interaction is omitted, its support meets the outer remainder, so its anchor lies within $\ell+2R+1$ layers of one of the $d$ outer faces. Counting at most $d(k-1)$ internal seams and $d$ outer faces bounds the omitted anchors per shape by $d(2R+1)(L/\ell)(L+2R)^{d-1}+d(\ell+2R+1)(L+2R)^{d-1}$. Therefore $\sup_s|H_L(s)-H_{L,\ell}^{\rm cut}(s)|\le J_0d[(2R+1)(L/\ell)+\ell+2R+1](L+2R)^{d-1}$. [A1, F1, F3]

2.1 If two energies on a finite state set differ pointwise by at most $D$, their partition sums satisfy $e^{-\beta D}Z'\le Z\le e^{\beta D}Z'$, so their log partition sums differ by at most $\beta D$ using [F2]. The cut energy factorizes over the cubes and has zero-energy remainder, hence $Z_{L,\ell}^{\rm cut}=Z_\ell^{k^d}q^{L^d-k^d\ell^d}$. Divide the comparison by $L^d$ and let $L\to\infty$ with $\ell$ fixed; the remainder fraction tends to zero, $k^d/L^d\to\ell^{-d}$, and the energy error has limsup at most $2^{d-1}\beta J_0d(2R+1)/\ell$. [A1, F1, F2, F3, step 1.2]

3.1 It follows for every $\ell>2R$ that $\limsup_L p_L\le p_\ell+2^{d-1}\beta J_0d(2R+1)/\ell$ and $\liminf_L p_L\ge p_\ell-2^{d-1}\beta J_0d(2R+1)/\ell$. Thus $0\le\limsup_Lp_L-\liminf_Lp_L\le2^d\beta J_0d(2R+1)/\ell$ for every such $\ell$. Letting $\ell\to\infty$ makes the difference zero; boundedness from step 1.1 then gives a finite limit. [A1, F1, step 1.1, step 2.1]

4.1 For $\widetilde H_L$, the finite-state comparison of step 2.1 gives $|L^{-d}\log\widetilde Z_L-p_L|\le\beta C_b/L$, which tends to zero. Its limit is therefore the same. [A1, F2, step 2.1, step 3.1] ∎

## Statement

Use the finite-alphabet, bounded, translation-invariant finite-range lattice model of [[def-tdmath-bounded-finite-range-lattice]], with physical interaction energies in joules, inverse temperature $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}>0$, and partition sum $Z_L(\beta)$. Suppose each site represents a fixed cell of volume $v_0>0$ in $\mathrm{m^3}$. Define the reduced log-partition density $p_L=L^{-d}\log Z_L$ and the lattice pressure convention $P_L=(k_{\mathrm B}T/v_0)p_L$ in pascals. Then $p_L$ and $P_L$ have finite limits as $L\to\infty$. If a second boundary-energy model on the same configuration sets differs pointwise by at most $C_bL^{d-1}$ joules for fixed $C_b$, it has the same limit.

The pressure convention in this statement is assigned to this lattice model. Equating it with a derivative-based macroscopic pressure or a measured mechanical pressure requires a separate model identification.

**Given:** A finite alphabet, finite-range bounded lattice interactions, positive $T$, the canonical partition sum, and a fixed physical cell volume.

[F1] [[def-tdmath-bounded-finite-range-lattice]]: for integer $d,L\ge1$, finite alphabet $\mathcal A$, bounded finite-range translation-invariant interactions, and $\beta>0$, $H_L$ and $Z_L=\sum_s e^{-\beta H_L(s)}$ are defined with free boundary.

[F2] [[thm-tdmath-finite-range-lattice-pressure-limit]] (current batch 11 draft): the sequence $p_L=L^{-d}\log Z_L$ has a finite limit for every fixed $\beta>0$, and a boundary-energy perturbation bounded by $C_bL^{d-1}$ has the same limit. Its full current proof was inspected; its draft status remains conditional.

[F3] [[def-td-si-quantities]]: $k_{\mathrm B}$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, $T$ is in kelvins, $v_0$ is in $\mathrm{m^3}$, and $k_{\mathrm B}T/v_0$ is in pascals.

[F4] [[post-td-canonical-sampling]]: the positive finite lattice partition sum defines the adopted finite-volume canonical law.

[A1] $v_0$ is fixed as $L$ varies, and the physical interaction parameters are held fixed in the sequence of cubic boxes.

## Proof

**Given:** The bounded finite-range lattice data, $\beta>0$, a fixed cell volume, and the stated boundary perturbation bound.

1.1 The finite lattice data in [F1] and $\beta>0$ match the model hypotheses of [F2]. Thus $p_L=L^{-d}\log Z_L$ converges to a finite $p_\infty$; the same supplier gives the identical limit for the stated boundary perturbation. By [F4], these finite partition sums give the adopted lattice canonical law. [F1, F2, F4, A1]

2.1 Since $v_0$ and $T$ are fixed along the volume sequence, multiplying by the constant $k_{\mathrm B}T/v_0$ preserves convergence: $P_L=(k_{\mathrm B}T/v_0)p_L\to(k_{\mathrm B}T/v_0)p_\infty$. ## Statement

For the lattice models of [[thm-tdmath-finite-range-lattice-pressure-limit]], write $p_L(\gamma)=L^{-d}\log Z_L(\gamma)$ and let $p(\gamma)=\lim_Lp_L(\gamma)$ on an open interval $J\subseteq(0,\infty)$. At finite $L$, use the canonical law $\mathbb P_{\gamma,L}(s):=e^{-\gamma H_L(s)}/Z_L(\gamma)$ and its finite expectation $\mathbb E_{\gamma,L}$. If $p$ is differentiable at $\beta\in J$, then $\mathbb E_{\beta,L}[H_L]/L^d\to e:=-p'(\beta)$. For every $\varepsilon>0$ there are $c>0$ and $L_0$ such that for $L\ge L_0$, $\mathbb P_{\beta,L}(|H_L/L^d-e|\ge\varepsilon)\le2e^{-cL^d}$. No energy-density limit is asserted at a nondifferentiability point.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** As stated in the item.

[A1] $J\subseteq(0,\infty)$ is open; the finite-volume canonical laws use $\mathbb P_{\gamma,L}(s)=e^{-\gamma H_L(s)}/Z_L(\gamma)$; $p_L(\gamma)\to p(\gamma)$ for each $\gamma\in J$; and $p$ is differentiable at the specified $\beta\in J$.

[F1] [[thm-tdmath-finite-range-lattice-pressure-limit]]: $p_L(\gamma)$ converges to finite $p(\gamma)$ for every $\gamma\in J$.

[F2] [[def-finite-probability-space-and-event]] and [[def-expectation-on-a-finite-probability-space]]: the finite-volume canonical weights define probabilities and expectations as finite sums.

[F3] [[def-variance-and-covariance]]: variance is a nonnegative centered second moment.

[F4] [[def-real-exponential-function-and-e]], [[thm-derivative-of-exponential]], [[def-natural-logarithm]], and [[thm-logarithm-derivative-and-integral]]: the exponential is smooth, its derivative is itself, its values are positive by the logarithm inverse convention, and $\log$ differentiates as $1/x$ on positive values. The series definition gives $\exp(0)=1$.

[F5] [[cor-mean-value-theorem]]: if $f$ is continuous on $[a,b]$ and differentiable on $(a,b)$, with $a<b$, then $f(b)-f(a)=f'(c)(b-a)$ for some $c\in(a,b)$.

[F6] [[thm-chain-rule]] and [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]: derivatives of compositions, finite sums, products and quotients obey the stated rules; quotients require a nonzero denominator.

[F7] [[thm-exponential-addition-formula]] and [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]]: $\exp(u+v)=\exp(u)\exp(v)$ for real $u,v$, and logarithms convert positive products and quotients to sums and differences.

## Proof

**Given:** The finite-volume lattice models, their canonical probabilities, pointwise convergence $p_L\to p$ on $J$, and differentiability of $p$ at $\beta$.

1.1 At every $\gamma\in J$, finite differentiation gives $p_L'(\gamma)=-L^{-d}\mathbb E_{\gamma,L}H_L$ and $p_L''(\gamma)=L^{-d}\operatorname{Var}_{\gamma,L}(H_L)\ge0$; these derivatives are continuous since the finite partition sum is smooth and positive. Apply [F5] to $p_L'$ on $[a,b]\subset J$: $p_L'(b)-p_L'(a)=p_L''(c)(b-a)\ge0$, so $p_L'$ is nondecreasing. For $a<b<c$ in $J$, apply [F5] to $p_L$ on $[a,b]$ and $[b,c]$. Their secant slopes are derivative values respectively below and above $b$, hence the left slope is no greater than the right. Rearrangement gives $p_L(b)\le[(c-b)p_L(a)+(b-a)p_L(c)]/(c-a)$, the convexity inequality. Passing this inequality to the pointwise limit proves convexity of $p$. [A1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6]

1.2 Fix $t>0$ small enough that $\beta\pm t\in J$. Since $\exp'=\exp>0$ and $\exp(0)=1$, [F5] gives $\exp(u)\ge1$ for $u\ge0$. For the upper tail, the pointwise inequality $\mathbf1_{\{H_L\ge L^d(e+\varepsilon)\}}\le e^{t(H_L-L^d(e+\varepsilon))}$ and finite summation give $\mathbb P(H_L/L^d\ge e+\varepsilon)\le\exp\{L^d[p_L(\beta-t)-p_L(\beta)-t(e+\varepsilon)]\}$. Differentiability of $p$ and $e=-p'(\beta)$ imply $p(\beta-t)=p(\beta)+te+o(t)$; choose $t$ so $|p(\beta-t)-p(\beta)-te|\le t\varepsilon/4$ and $|p(\beta+t)-p(\beta)+te|\le t\varepsilon/4$. Thus the upper bracket's limit is at most $-3t\varepsilon/4$. Pointwise convergence at $\beta-t$ and $\beta$ then makes the bracket at most $-t\varepsilon/2$ for all sufficiently large $L$. [A1, F1, F2, F4, F5, F7]

2.1 For any small $h>0$ with $\beta\pm h\in J$, apply [F5] to $p_L$ on $[\beta-h,\beta]$ and $[\beta,\beta+h]$. Each secant slope is a value of $p_L'$ on its respective open interval, so the monotonicity in step 1.1 gives $[p_L(\beta)-p_L(\beta-h)]/h\le p_L'(\beta)\le[p_L(\beta+h)-p_L(\beta)]/h$. Take lower and upper limits in $L$, use [F1], then let $h\downarrow0$; differentiability of $p$ forces $p_L'(\beta)\to p'(\beta)$. The identity in step 1.1 yields the claimed mean limit. [A1, F1, F5, step 1.1]

2.2 For the lower tail use $\mathbf1_{\{H_L\le L^d(e-\varepsilon)\}}\le e^{-t(H_L-L^d(e-\varepsilon))}$; its expectation is $\exp\{L^d[p_L(\beta+t)-p_L(\beta)+t(e-\varepsilon)]\}$. For the same $t$ chosen in step 1.2, the bracket has limit at most $-3t\varepsilon/4$; increasing $L_0$ therefore makes this at most $e^{-L^dt\varepsilon/2}$. Adding both tail bounds yields the result with $c=t\varepsilon/2$. [A1, F1, F2, F4, F7, step 1.2]

3.1 Steps 1.2–2.2 bound the two tails whose union is $\{|H_L/L^d-e|\ge\varepsilon\}$; the theorem is conditional on differentiability of $p$ and does not assert convergence of second derivatives or equivalence for arbitrary observables. [A1, step 1.2, step 2.2] ∎
